name: OnEMI Technology Solutions Ltd
title: OnEMI Technology Solutions Ltd - 544754 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Digital consumer lender (Kissht) guiding AUM growth above 40% and ROA 4.5-5% for FY27 while yields compress; asset quality improving on GNPA 2.12%, but the headline GNPA drop is a write-off policy change, not pure credit improvement.

summary.headline: Kissht (OnEMI) FY26 AUM rose 73% YoY to ₹7,066 crore; GNPA fell to 2.12% and FY26 PAT grew 75% to ₹281 crore.
summary.overview: First earnings call since the May 8, 2026 listing. AUM grew 19% QoQ to ₹7,066 crore and PAT grew 52% YoY and 7% QoQ in Q4. Asset quality improved, with GNPA down 77 bps YoY to 2.12% and Stage-3 ECL coverage at 86.2%. Management deliberately reduced yields to target higher-quality borrowers, which compressed the Q3-to-Q4 margin, and guided to FY27 AUM growth above 40%, ROA of 4.5-5% and ROE of 19-21%.

financial_highlights.metric: Impairment cost as % of average AUM

segments.name: Personal loans (unsecured, on-book and off-book)
segments.commentary: On-book AUM ₹3,556 crore and off-book AUM ₹3,510 crore, with off-book covered by FLDG capped at 5%. Disbursements were cut about 7% and about 450 pin codes were paused on early-warning flags.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹518 crore across 98 branches in 8 states, or 7.3% of AUM. LTV is about 48% and expected to stay range-bound. LAP is not yet at breakeven and is about 1-2 years from steady-state ROA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth above 40%, with secured book scale-up expected to be strong.
Gross NPA below 2.25%, impairment costs down 10-15% YoY, and continued Stage-1 mix improvement.
Return on average AUM of 4.5-5%, which implies ROE of 19-21%. Guidance is for FY27 alone.
Yield is expected to keep declining over the next four to six quarters at a pace similar to Q3-to-Q4. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term and 14-16% in three to four quarters.
Cost of borrowing fell about 200 bps after the Crisil A- upgrade in February 2026; a further upgrade in FY27 could cut it another 100-150 bps in FY28.
LAP: at least 80 more branches by end of FY27, with calibrated expansion in Karnataka, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, UP and Maharashtra.
No disbursement guidance for FY27; guidance is on AUM growth.
capex_capacity: IPO proceeds: 75% of primary issue (about ₹630 crore) already infused as equity into NBFC subsidiary Si Creva Capital; balance 25% for general corporate purposes including technology, AI, brand and customer acquisition.
Capital position described as comfortable for 40% AUM growth in FY27; no near-term fundraise indicated.
Collections team expanded in Q4 FY26, mainly on the field side, with a dedicated NPA recovery team. Operating base: over 7,000 field agents and 1,000+ tele-callers.
Steady-state on-book debt-to-equity seen at 2.5-3x; off-book leverage not a constraint since only the 5% FLDG is blocked.
New wholly-owned subsidiary created to distribute mutual funds and wealth products.
demand_pricing: Margin compression is deliberate: yields reduced to win higher-quality, lower-risk borrowers, with benefits from operating leverage and lower funding costs partly passed to customers.
Repeat customers: 11.76 million unique customers to date, about 3.5 million active; repeat share supports growth.
Acquisition: digital marketing under 50% of acquisition, partner channels (merchants, e-commerce, aggregators) about 55%, organic about 30%.
Competition cited as Bajaj and Chola; management points to credit performance and repeat-customer base as edge.
Borrowing cost on-book ranged 11.5%-14.25% across 45+ lenders.

qa_highlights.question: Rating upgrade outlook and impact on borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Crisil rated A- in Feb 2026 and India Ratings A- in Nov 2025. About 200 bps lower marginal cost of borrowing already seen since the Crisil upgrade. Another upgrade is possible in FY27 (discussion over next 6-8 months), worth a further 100-150 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA so much higher than two years ago (0.79% to 2.89%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a technical change: the write-off period was extended from 120 to 150 days after discussion with auditors. GNPA has been stable on the 150-day basis for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPEX rise and other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP not yet at breakeven and branch additions; plus a one-time Q4 investment in field collections staff for FY27 recoveries. Other income fell sequentially with a small margin compression.

qa_highlights.question: What is the portfolio yield and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 portfolio yield about 30-31%, 50-75 bps below Q3. Management expects a similar downward trend for four to six quarters. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is FLDG capped at 5% and can lenders push IRR above it?
qa_highlights.answer: Contractual risk is capped at 5% FLDG. Lenders may negotiate on hurdle rates, but the exposure does not extend beyond the FLDG.

qa_highlights.question: How is AUM growth changing the ROA and secured-mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall AUM growth above 40%. The 4.5% ROA guidance covers the whole book, with secured lending at lower ROA. Management expects secured to reach roughly 19-21% ROE over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and AUM growth accelerate QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher-quality customers at lower rates, plus repeat customers from the 3.5 million active base. Management says April-May momentum continues.

risks_watch: Yield compression is guided to continue for four to six quarters; ROA of 4.5-5% depends on funding-cost and opex offsets.
LAP is loss-making at the margin and needs 1-2 years to reach steady-state ROA; 80 new branches add opex.
Stage-3 and gross NPA trends depend on the 150-day write-off policy; a change in policy would shift the reported number.
Off-book book depends on FLDG partner appetite and on negotiated lender hurdle rates.
Rating upgrade and resulting funding-cost cuts are not assured; timing depends on FY27 rating reviews.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and guidance, with explicit emphasis on prudence and ROA protection. Cautious on near-term margins, which management openly says will keep declining. Evasive on disbursement targets and on the exact origination yield for April-May.
key_quotes: And at this stage, we believe, Prudence ceases to be a conservative instinct - it becomes a genuine competitive advantage.
We would rather carry prudence slightly early than discover optimism slightly late.
Kissht is a technology company that does lending - not the other way around, a lending company that uses technology.

We are not building for the next quarter, rather, we are building for the next decade - with sharper judgments, stronger governance, deeper technology, and a balance sheet designed to compound through cycles, not merely benefit from favorable ones.

adds.what: At least 80 more LAP branches by end of FY27 (Karnataka, AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, UP, Maharashtra)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 AUM growth above 40% (revenue_growth_pct recorded as 40 as the midpoint proxy), backed partly by a LAP branch expansion of at least 80 branches by end FY27 and a repeat-customer base, but no sized capacity or contracted orders were given, and the 40% figure is AUM not revenue.
